title: Adapter and Bridge
idea: Adapter wraps an existing class so it fits the interface your code expects. Bridge splits an abstraction from its implementation so both can vary independently.
points: An adapter translates names, units and errors; it adds no new behaviour.
Your code depends on its own interface, never on the vendor's.
Bridge holds the implementation as a field, instead of subclassing every combination.
Adapter fixes a mismatch after the fact; Bridge is planned up front.

walk.text: Vendor code you cannot edit: amounts in cents, a result object.
The adapter wraps the vendor object it receives.
It converts units and renames the call.
It maps the vendor's result to your error and return shapes.
`checkout` knows only `pay`; swapping vendors means writing one new adapter.

code.title: Bridge: alerts and channels
code.caption: Add a `PushChannel` class with `deliver`. Both alert kinds work with it unchanged.

walk.text: Implementations: each channel delivers text its own way; SMS trims to 16 characters.
The abstraction holds a channel, the bridge, and delegates to it.
Refine the abstraction by subclassing `Alert`; channels are untouched.
Any alert pairs with any channel at runtime.

pitfalls: Keep business rules out of adapters; they only translate between two shapes.
Do not leak vendor types or error codes past the adapter.
Skip the Bridge when only one dimension varies; one class holding a channel field is enough.

quiz.why: The adapter calls the wrapped `read()`, gets 20, and converts it: 20 × 9 / 5 + 32 is 68.

takeaway: Adapter makes a misfit class fit; Bridge keeps two dimensions apart.
